A1.justification: Both PDFs contain readable main texts, equations, figures, tables, and complete supplementary material for the same Skip-DiT work. Despite the changed title and substantial reorganization, retained methods and experiments can be matched reliably.

before.justification: v1 reports original image/video generation experiments, feature-smoothness analyses, caching ablations, and ImageNet training and acceleration results in Appendix 6.

after.justification: v3 retains original generation experiments and adds training-checkpoint results, cached-feature stability measurements, and additional baseline evaluations.

M1.justification: v1 describes fixed 1:N feature reuse within selected timestep ranges. v3 Section 3.5 and Algorithm 1 add accumulated errors from static records R and threshold-triggered early cache refresh. The concatenation–LayerNorm–linear skip architecture and two-stage training strategy remain unchanged; the spectral-constraint terminology does not specify a separate new normalization or training operation.

E1.justification: Both versions cover FaceForensics, SkyTimelapse, UCF101, Taichi-HD, Vimeo-2M text-to-video training, ImageNet class-to-image generation, and COCO text-to-image evaluation. ImageNet experiments already appear in v1 Appendix 6. Their greater prominence and the additional analyses in v3 do not establish new dataset or generation-task coverage.

E2.justification: v3 Table 2 adds AdaCache and TeaCache to the text-to-video comparison in v1 Table 3. v3 Appendix Table 8 adds the comparator labeled Faster-Diff at both classifier-free guidance settings, and Figure 3 compares its cached-feature stability alongside FORA. These additions substantially broaden the evaluated comparison methods.

E3.justification: v3 adds intermediate-checkpoint evaluation from 400k to 2.9M training steps and cached-versus-full feature-similarity testing, while retaining the final training budget and most benchmark protocols. Appendix 9 newly states 25-step DDPM for class-to-image sampling, conflicting with the 250 steps retained in Tables 7–8; this discrepancy does not establish that the sampler actually changed.

E4.justification: v1's Taichi parameter-perturbation landscapes at DDPM steps 10 and 250 are replaced by class-to-image and text-to-video landscapes in v3 Figure 2. v3 also adds sample-wise caching-stability analysis and longitudinal training-convergence analysis in Figures 3–4. The cache-range, compatibility, and DDIM-comparison experiments remain, while the vanilla-Latte heatmap panel is removed.

E5.justification: v3 Figure 3 newly reports mean and standard deviation across samples for cached-output cosine similarity. v1's corresponding stability visualizations do not report sample spread. This is a limited uncertainty-reporting addition; neither version supplies repeated-training-run counts, seed information, or confidence intervals for the benchmark tables.

E6.justification: v3 adds a training trajectory, including FID 9.07 at 1.6M steps, beyond v1's retained 2.9M-step endpoint of 8.37, plus results for the added baselines. Latte PAB235/347/469 VBench scores change from 73.79/72.08/71.64 to 73.77/71.11/70.20. Most existing Skip-DiT benchmark values remain unchanged. The text-to-image speedup prose changes from 2.28× to 2.09×, matching the unchanged Table 4, and one appendix qualitative-example row is replaced.

T1.justification: v1 provides diffusion, feature-similarity, and caching equations without formal stability theorems. v3 Sections 3.4–3.5 and Appendix 6 introduce homogeneous contractive-block assumptions, Theorem 1 concerning Jacobian spectral norms and stability/convergence, and Theorem 2 concerning accumulated reuse errors and allowable caching intervals, with accompanying proofs.

C1.justification: v3 expands the central contribution from feature-smoothness-based inference acceleration to identifying Dynamic Feature Instability as an architectural cause of inefficient training and unstable caching, with claimed theoretical guarantees. Training efficiency, already discussed in v1's appendix, becomes a headline 4.4× acceleration claim based on 1.6M versus 7M steps, rather than the earlier reported approximately 38% training cost.

C2.justification: v1 explains caching benefits through smoother features and U-Net-like information preservation. v3 attributes instability, error amplification, and slow convergence to uncontrolled Jacobian spectral norms, and interprets the convergence results as confirming spectral control through long skip connections. It also develops the rationale for static caching instead of sample-dependent adaptation. These are substantive new mechanism interpretations.

D1.justification: v3 supplies AdaCache's Latte codebook, TeaCache's slow-caching setting, perturbation coefficients, and an explicit 50k-image ImageNet evaluation count. Conversely, it omits v1's 8-fps training-video specification and Hunyuan prompt-enhancement and 1024-to-256 resizing instructions. These are documentation changes, not evidence that the underlying preprocessing changed. Existing repository access and most hardware/configuration disclosures remain.

R1.justification: v3 adds adaptive-caching literature, including AdaCache and TeaCache, and training/stability work including ScaleLong, FasterDiT, Dynamic Diffusion Transformer, and spectral normalization/regularization. It removes the earlier loss-landscape references. Positioning shifts substantially from improving inference caching through feature smoothness to explaining architectural causes of training and inference instability.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, introduction, contribution statements, and methodological narrative are extensively rewritten. Skip branches become Long-Skip-Connections, and Skip-Cache is largely renamed Skip-DiT with cached inference. Image-generation results receive a reorganized main-text section, while scheduler discussion moves into the supplement. This goes beyond adding scientific content.

P2.justification: v3 replaces the qualitative opening montage with a three-panel analytical overview, incorporates a revised architecture diagram, adds stability and convergence plots, and redraws the heatmap with changed axes and one panel. Tables are regrouped and resized; the DDIM table moves to the appendix and existing class-to-image results are also displayed in the main text. Most appendix imagery is retained, with one example row replaced.

improvement.justification: The added checkpoint results and baseline comparisons strengthen the empirical evidence, and the text-to-image speedup correction improves consistency. However, the newly central theoretical guarantees concern an idealized convex-combination skip model without establishing their applicability to Equation 4's learned concatenation–normalization–linear mapping. The conflicting 25/250-step sampler statements and removed preprocessing details also weaken reproducibility. These empirical benefits and substantive rigor/reporting concerns prevent a reliable net quality judgment.
